content.text: ▪︎MC; MC mech: inversion of a plantar-flexed foot; most involve only the ATFL (stronger forces → all 3 lat ligaments)
▪︎eversion of a plantar-flexed foot more likely → avulsion frx of medial malleolus (deltoid lig = strong)
➀ syndesmotic ligament (connects tibia & fibula in the lower leg)
▪︎mech: external rotation, forceful dorsiflexion; less common than lat sprains
: pain, swelling, ecchymosis, limited ROM, ⇡ joint laxity, impaired or unable to bear wt
▪︎syndesmotic: tenderness at distal tibiofibular joint; pain more proximal, above the ankle joint
Grade I: stretching & microscopic tears; ⍉instability, able to bear wt + ambulate, minimal swelling + tenderness
Grade II: lrger but incomplete tear; moderate pain, swelling, tenderness + ecchymosis; mild-mod instability; pain w/ wt-bearing + ambulation
Grade III: complete tear; significant pain + instability; unable to bear wt or ambulate
▪︎ankle XR if pain in malleolar zone + any: bone tenderness at posterior edge (distal 6cm) or tip of lat malleolus, or of medial malleolus; inability to bear wt for 4 steps (immediately + at eval)
▪︎foot XR if pain in midfoot zone + any: bone tenderness at base of 5th metatarsal or navicular; inability to bear wt for 4 steps (immediately + at eval)
▪︎RICE (lacking formal studies); oral or topical NSAIDs for pain; early ROM exercises; functional bracing + functional rehab
▪︎emerging: MEAT (movement, exercise, analgesia, treatment) or MOVE (movement, options, vary, ease)
▪︎grade I: bear wt as tolerated, PT
▪︎grade II: LE splint or walking boot (or air splint), PT
▪︎syndesmotic: immobilize, non-wt-bearing; possible surg for grade 2/3
: ⍉resolution w/ conservative, severe grade III lat sprains, deltoid disrupt, ↑ankle sprain, chronic ankle instability
▪︎frx of prox fibula + tear of tibiofibular syndesmosis + interosseous membrane
▪︎MC mech: external rotation of the foot relative to the tibia
▪︎XR: spiral frx of prox fibula; disruption of tibiofibular syndesmosis
▪︎long leg posterior splint w/ reduction of medial ankle
as it travels thru the tarsal tunnel; compress may be a result of overuse, restrictive footwear, or edematous states
(ex, alternating pain/numbness @ medial malleolus, heel, & sole); does
▪︎pain ⇡ throughout day, worsens @ night & w/ dorsiflexion
: conservative (ex, rest, NSAIDs, properly fitted shoes, orthotics)
